business_rules: Chat requires BOTH parties to hold a plan with the `chat` feature (canChat). One-sided is not enough.
Chat messages never create a Notification. Unread chat is a separate badge.
Connection is DERIVED, never stored: an accepted BookingRequest OR an accepted Application.
Exactly ONE Conversation per (company, freelancer) pair, always via ensureConversation().
Duplicate booking requests are blocked when connected, UNLESS scoped to a new requirement_id.
One application per requirement per freelancer (DB unique index).
Public profiles use an ALLOW-LIST, never a deny-list. Email, phone and coordinates can never leak.
Without a subscription the professional's identity is withheld SERVER-SIDE (name, photo, bio, equipment, social links, gallery).
Requirements default to `draft`; only `published` ones accept applications.
Only `available` availability blocks are bookable; a non-bookable block excludes the freelancer from date-filtered search.
Money is INTEGER PAISE. Never floats. fee + net === gross must hold exactly.
Ledger entries are IMMUTABLE - corrections are new ADJUSTMENT/REVERSAL rows.
Balances are DERIVED from the ledger, never stored on a user.
Payments only between connected parties.
FAILED payments can never become SUCCESS - a retry is a NEW payment.
Webhooks are the authoritative payment confirmation, not the browser.
Withdrawals debit on REQUEST (not completion) so concurrent requests cannot overdraw; failure posts a REVERSAL.
Payout identifiers are select:false; only `masked` is ever returned.
Activity logging must never break a business operation - logActivity never throws.
Never log or store: passwords, JWTs, API secrets, full bank/UPI identifiers, private emails/phones, message bodies.
Legacy data is never destroyed - unmatched master-data values are flagged needs_master_review.

safe_development_rules: Inspect existing code before changing anything.
Preserve existing functionality; the site is in production use.
Do not rebuild existing systems unnecessarily.
Reuse existing components and the authority services.
Follow the existing architecture (controller -> service -> model).
Do not delete functionality without explicit instruction.
Do not change database structure unnecessarily.
Do not reset MongoDB - real user data exists.
Run the E2E suites after changes (509 assertions is the baseline).
Run `npm run build` in frontend/ after any frontend change.
Verify the backend starts after any backend change.
Perform regression testing across all nine suites.
If something conflicts with a requested feature, explain the conflict before making a destructive change.
